title: General Catalyst leads $1.1B round into 2-month-old River AI
slides: Can a two-month-old startup justify $1.1 billion?
General Catalyst led the round, valuing River AI.
The company has zero revenue and no public product.
This bet forces rivals to rethink AI funding timelines.
Watch for River's first release to validate the price.
thread_text:
1. Why so much?

Two-month-old River AI just got a $1.1 billion price tag from General Catalyst, with zero revenue and no public product.

2. The bet's real message

Rivals now face a stark choice: chase valuations or wait for proof. The funding timeline just compressed.

3. What's behind the curtain

No product means investors are betting on the team and idea alone. It's a leap, not a step.

4. Pressure to deliver

River's first release will either justify the hype or burst the bubble. Every move is scrutinized.

5. Your move

Before the next big AI bet, ask yourself: would you invest in a promise this raw? Test that logic on your next project.
video_script: First release will prove or lose it.

instagram.caption:
A two-month-old startup with zero revenue and no public product just raised $1.1 billion. General Catalyst led the round, betting purely on the team and the idea. No leaks, no demo, no roadmap. 🎯

That's the whole pitch. For founders and creators building in AI, this changes the calculus: the timeline to a massive valuation just compressed overnight. If a blank-slate startup can land this, the bar for "proof" has officially moved. 📉

For anyone making content or tools with AI, expect more aggressive funding cycles—and more pressure to ship before you're ready. River's first release will be the real test. ⏳

Would you take that bet on your next project? 💸
